content.text: I have reviewed every section. No audit, inspection, or verification right binding the Client exists anywhere in the agreement.

input.quote: Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: TrueLink has no audit, inspection, verification or records-access right against us anywhere in the agreement. The only information-flow mechanics run in our favour: Section 6 obliges TrueLink to give us supporting documentation for its charges and a right to contest them, and Section 3(e) gives us real-time access to Interface usage statistics and raw log files. Fees are billed by TrueLink invoice under Section 5(a), so there is no self-reporting regime that would call for verification. The only TrueLink monitoring language, Section 8(f)'s reservation of the right to implement technical mechanisms to prevent "spamming," operates on TrueLink's own hosted environment and is neither an audit of our records nor access to our systems (and is the subject of the separate anti-spam covenant, not this rule). Because no audit right exists, we are in a position better than the preferred position (which merely caps frequency, notice, cost and system access), so there is nothing to redline; inserting audit machinery would only create a Vendor right we do not currently face. Noted for the file rather than flagged: if the pricing exhibits are later completed with per-transaction self-reported volumes, we should confirm no audit right is added and, if one is proposed, hold it to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site, independent auditor, at TrueLink's cost absent 5% underpayment.
